Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: Support-only synthesis; no new primary MLA standard

A school fundraiser has a $120 setup cost and earns $8 per item sold. Which expression represents profit after x items?

feedback.text: Correct. Profit is revenue minus the fixed setup cost.
This treats the setup cost as a per-item rate.
This gives total revenue plus cost, not profit.
This subtracts earnings from the cost, reversing the profit relationship.

A data model predicts 42.6 students will attend a workshop. What is the most reasonable interpretation?

feedback.text: People must be counted with whole numbers, so this is not realistic.
Correct. The model output should be rounded to a reasonable whole-number count.
This moves the decimal point and greatly changes the prediction.
The prediction is positive, so zero does not match the model.

Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: Support-only synthesis; no new primary MLA standard

Which choice best describes a useful model for a real-world situation?

feedback.text: Units are essential for interpreting the result.

answer.text: A model that always gives whole numbers

feedback.text: Some contexts use decimals, such as money, measurements, or rates.

answer.text: A model that fits the context and gives interpretable results

feedback.text: Correct. A useful model must connect mathematics to the situation.

answer.text: A model that never needs checking

feedback.text: Every model should be checked against data, constraints, and assumptions.

Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: Support-only synthesis; no new primary MLA standard

A population grows by 6% each year from an initial value of 500. Which model is appropriate?

feedback.text: This is linear growth, not percent growth each year.
This makes the initial amount part of the base instead of the starting value.
This represents a 6% decrease, not growth.
Correct. Growth by 6% uses a factor of 1.06 each year.

Question ID: ALG2_U06_L07_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: Support-only synthesis; no new primary MLA standard

Two models fit a data set. Model A has residuals mostly near 0, while Model B has residuals that form a clear curve. Which model is better supported?

answer.text: Model A, because residuals near 0 with no pattern suggest a better fit

feedback.text: Correct. Random residuals close to 0 support the model choice.

answer.text: Model B, because a curved residual pattern proves the model is exact

feedback.text: A residual pattern usually means the chosen model misses structure in the data.

answer.text: Model B, because larger residuals are always better

feedback.text: Large residuals indicate larger prediction errors.

answer.text: Neither model can ever be compared

feedback.text: Models can be compared using residuals, context, and prediction accuracy.
